newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges caution over herbal cures for AIDS.
newsitem.headline: China urges caution over herbal cures for AIDS.

text.p: China warned on Sunday that its researchers seeking a herbal cure for AIDS should be cautious before announcing major breakthroughs.

"We are fully convinced that China's traditional herbal medicines can contribute significantly to global AIDS control, if we continue conducting rigorous and scientific research on it," the Xinhua news agency quoted Kang Laiyi, director of the Shanghai Municipal AIDS Surveillance Centre, as saying.

However, while Chinese herbal medicines offered hope to the campaign to fight AIDS, Kang said China's pharmacologists should gather more evidence about their effectiveness before announcing major breakthroughs.
China had reported 4,305 HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) cases by the end of August, including 131 patients with full-blown AIDS, Xinhua said. It said 86 AIDS patients in China had died.
The human immunodeficiency virus HIV leads to Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), and while there is no cure for AIDS, several have been found to work against HIV.

The results of animal experiments, cytological research and clinical use conducted by a research group led by Kang had shown that a locally-developed AIDS medicine was partially effective as a treatment for AIDS, Kang said.
The medicine was found to generally improve the immune systems of animals without long or short-term toxic effects, he said.

Clinical use of the medicine on several AIDS patients showed their symptoms had been clearly alleviated and the functions of their immune systems were resuming, he said. HIV had not appeared in their blood and the antigen P24 had vanished, he said.
"Although we're still detecting HIV rna (ribonucleic acid) in the patients' blood, the medicine has shown the sign of having a curative effect on aids," Kang said.
Chinese state media have frequently said they have made breakthroughs in findings cures for AIDS, but apparently no independent assessment has been issued to back up those announcements.
"We should make further studies and establish more convincing facts before we reach the final conclusion," Kang cautioned of his findings.

Kang, a member of the National Prevention and Control Committee of AIDS Experts, urged local researchers to develop a still more serious attitude toward conducting accurate AIDS drug research using herbal medicine.
"We should keep a tight control on medicine quality, conduct...clinical experiments and establish detailed observation indexes," he said.
Developing effective but affordable drugs to treat AIDS was an important task, he said.
